chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a dispute regarding a man who had taken a fleeing slave and kept him with him, then the slave escaped from him. He (AS) said: 'He swears by Allah, the One there is no god but Him, that he did not strip him of his clothes, nor take anything that was on him, nor sell him, nor be lenient in releasing him. If he swears, he is free from liability.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a person who captures a fleeing slave and the slave later escapes?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the conditions for absolving the captor of financial liability (ضمان) when holding a fleeing slave, emphasizing that the exemption applies only if the slave's original state—clothing and possessions—remains intact and no undue delay occurred. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that retention of a slave is a form of temporary custody rather than immediate ownership, requiring the holder to preserve the slave's assets and release them promptly upon claim. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of manumission, linking the legal status of the 'abiq' to the broader ethical obligations of fair treatment before eventual freedom.
